sets.title: Four days, full pay
sets.instructions: Read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
sets.passage:
When a Valencian software firm announced that its staff would work four days a week on full pay, many observers (1) ____ the idea as a publicity stunt. Two years on, the company has not only kept its clients but has also (2) ____ the envy of far larger rivals, who now find their best developers applying for jobs there.

Supporters of the model argue that a compressed week forces teams to (3) ____ priorities with unusual rigour. Meetings that once dragged on for an hour are now capped at twenty minutes, and any task that does not (4) ____ directly to a project's goals is quietly dropped. Managers also report that employees are less likely to (5) ____ out, and that the atmosphere in the office is noticeably calmer than it used to be.

Critics, however, point out that the arrangement is far easier to adopt in knowledge-based industries than in sectors where someone must physically be present at all times. Hospitals, (6) ____, cannot simply close their wards on a Friday and hope for the best. There is also the (7) ____ possibility that working hours become so intense that the free day turns into a recovery period rather than genuine leisure time.

Whatever its limitations, the experiment has (8) ____ a much broader debate about what productivity really means. If output matters more than hours logged, then perhaps the traditional office week deserves the same scrutiny that companies routinely apply to every other cost.

items.prompt: Gap (1)
items.explanation: La estructura fija es 'dismiss something as + sustantivo' (descartar algo por considerarlo...). 'Refuse' y 'decline' no admiten 'as' con este sentido, y 'neglect' significa desatender, no despreciar una idea.

items.prompt: Gap (2)
items.explanation: La expresión fija es 'become the envy of' (convertirse en la envidia de). 'Turn' no funciona con artículo + sustantivo aquí, y 'come'/'grow' no forman esta colocación.

items.prompt: Gap (3)
items.explanation: La colocación natural es 'set priorities' (fijar prioridades). 'Lay', 'put' y 'place' no se combinan con 'priorities' en este sentido ('place priority on' existe, pero en singular y con 'on').

items.prompt: Gap (4)
items.explanation: 'Contribute to' (contribuir a) es el único verbo que rige 'to' con este significado. 'Support' y 'assist' son transitivos sin 'to', y 'add to' significa aumentar algo, no ayudar a alcanzar objetivos.

items.prompt: Gap (5)
items.explanation: 'Burn out' es el phrasal verb para el agotamiento laboral (burnout). 'Wash out' (desteñirse, suspenderse por lluvia), 'cut out' (apagarse un motor) y 'break out' (estallar) no se aplican a personas agotadas.

items.prompt: Gap (6)
items.explanation: Los hospitales son un ejemplo de los sectores mencionados en la frase anterior, así que el conector correcto es 'for instance'. 'In turn' indica una consecuencia en cadena, 'even so' una concesión que contradiría la lógica y 'on the contrary' rechaza una afirmación previa.

items.prompt: Gap (7)
items.explanation: La colocación fija es 'a distinct possibility' (una posibilidad real). 'Sharp', 'plain' y 'bright' no se combinan con 'possibility'.

items.prompt: Gap (8)
items.explanation: 'Spark a debate' (desencadenar un debate) es la colocación correcta. 'Light' se usa con fuego o velas, y 'fire'/'burn' no se usan con 'debate'.

sets.title: The myth of multitasking
sets.instructions: Read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
sets.passage:
Most of us like to think that we can answer emails, follow a video call and draft a report all (1) ____ once. Neuroscientists, however, are increasingly convinced that what we call multitasking is (2) ____ more than rapid switching between tasks, and that each switch comes at a cost. (3) ____ time attention moves from one activity to another, the brain needs a moment to reorient itself, and these small delays add up over the course of a working day.

Technology companies are partly to blame. Notifications are designed to be difficult to ignore, (4) ____ is hardly surprising given that the business models of many apps depend (5) ____ capturing as much of our attention as possible. Some researchers estimate that office workers are interrupted every few minutes, and that it can take far longer than that to regain full concentration.

(6) ____ this mean we should abandon our devices altogether? Not necessarily. Experts suggest blocking out periods of the day during (7) ____ notifications are silenced, so that demanding work can be done without interruption. Those who have tried this approach often report that they get more done in a single focused morning (8) ____ in an entire distracted day.

items.prompt: Gap (1)
items.explanation: 'All at once' es una expresión fija que significa 'todo a la vez'.

items.prompt: Gap (2)
items.explanation: 'Nothing more than' (no es más que) es la estructura que expresa la idea; 'little more than' y 'no more than' también son válidos con un matiz casi idéntico.

items.prompt: Gap (3)
items.explanation: 'Every time' / 'Each time' (también 'Any time') funciona como conjunción temporal: cada vez que la atención cambia...

items.prompt: Gap (4)
items.explanation: Tras coma, 'which' introduce una relativa no especificativa que se refiere a toda la oración anterior. 'That' no puede usarse tras coma.

items.prompt: Gap (5)
items.explanation: 'Depend on/upon + -ing' es la preposición regida por el verbo.

items.prompt: Gap (6)
items.explanation: Se necesita el auxiliar para formar la pregunta en presente simple con sujeto singular ('this'): 'Does this mean...?'

items.prompt: Gap (7)
items.explanation: Tras preposición ('during') solo se puede usar 'which' para cosas; 'that' no puede seguir a una preposición.

items.prompt: Gap (8)
items.explanation: El comparativo 'more' exige 'than' para introducir el segundo término de la comparación.

sets.title: Reclaiming the city centre
sets.instructions: Read the text below. Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.
sets.passage:
Over the past decade, several European cities have tried to reclaim their centres from cars. The results have been (1) ____ encouraging. In Pontevedra, for example, the (2) ____ of the historic core led not to the economic decline that shopkeepers had feared but to a revival of local trade.

Such schemes are rarely (3) ____, however. Drivers often complain that restrictions are imposed without adequate (4) ____, and businesses that rely on deliveries worry about rising costs. City councils have learned that (5) ____ about the aims of a project is essential if residents are to accept short-term (6) ____.

Perhaps the most striking change is social. Streets that were once (7) ____ to anyone not inside a vehicle now host markets, children's games and outdoor cafés. Urban researchers argue that this (8) ____ cannot be measured purely in terms of traffic data, yet it is precisely what makes a city worth living in.

items.prompt: REMARK
items.explanation: Se necesita un adverbio que modifique al adjetivo 'encouraging': remark → remarkable → remarkably.

items.prompt: PEDESTRIAN
items.explanation: Tras 'the' y antes de 'of' hace falta un sustantivo: pedestrian → pedestrianise → pedestrianisation (peatonalización). Se aceptan ambas grafías.

items.prompt: CONTROVERSY
items.explanation: Adjetivo negativo: 'rarely uncontroversial' = casi siempre generan polémica, que encaja con las quejas que siguen. Requiere prefijo 'un-' y cambio de sustantivo a adjetivo.

items.prompt: CONSULT
items.explanation: Tras 'adequate' se necesita un sustantivo: 'consultation' (consulta pública). 'Consultancy' sería una empresa o servicio de asesoría, lo que no encaja.

items.prompt: TRANSPARENT
items.explanation: Hace falta un sustantivo como sujeto de 'is essential': transparent → transparency.

items.prompt: CONVENIENT
items.explanation: Sustantivo con prefijo negativo: los residentes deben aceptar molestias a corto plazo, 'short-term inconvenience'.

items.prompt: HOSPITABLE
items.explanation: El contraste con 'now host markets...' exige un adjetivo negativo: calles antes hostiles para quien no iba en coche. Prefijo 'in-'.

items.prompt: VIBRANT
items.explanation: Tras 'this' se necesita un sustantivo: vibrant → vibrancy (vitalidad, dinamismo).

sets.title: Key word transformations (Set 1)
sets.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.prompt: It wasn't necessary for you to send the report to the whole team. || NEED || You ____ the report to the whole team.
items.explanation: 'Needn't have + participio' indica que algo se hizo pero no era necesario, que es justo el sentido de la frase original.

items.prompt: The new software was so complicated that nobody could use it without training. || SUCH || It was ____ that nobody could use it without training.
accept: such a complicated piece of software
items.explanation: 'Such + (adjetivo) + sustantivo + that'. 'Software' es incontable, así que no lleva 'a' salvo que se use 'a piece of'.

items.prompt: I'm sure the manager didn't know about the delay. || HAVE || The manager ____ about the delay.
items.explanation: La deducción negativa segura sobre el pasado se expresa con 'can't/couldn't have + participio'. 'Mustn't have' no se usa para deducciones.

items.prompt: People say that the company is planning to relocate to Madrid. || SAID || The company ____ planning to relocate to Madrid.
items.explanation: Pasiva impersonal con sujeto personal: 'be said to + infinitivo'. Como la acción está en curso, se usa 'to be (planning)'.

items.prompt: She only realised how serious the problem was when the auditors arrived. || UNTIL || It was ____ that she realised how serious the problem was.
accept: not until the auditors had arrived
items.explanation: La estructura enfática 'It was not until... that...' equivale a 'only when'. Hay que conservar el sujeto 'the auditors' y el verbo en pasado.

items.prompt: The meeting was postponed because the CEO was ill. || ACCOUNT || The meeting was postponed ____ illness.
accept: on account of the chief executive's
items.explanation: 'On account of' (debido a) va seguido de un sintagma nominal, por eso se usa el posesivo 'the CEO's illness'.

sets.title: Cultivated meat: from lab to table?
sets.instructions: Read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
sets.passage:
When the first laboratory-grown burger was presented to the press, it cost a small fortune to produce and tasted, by most accounts, rather dry. Few people at the time (1) ____ it as anything more than a scientific curiosity. Since then, however, dozens of start-ups have (2) ____ up, backed by investors who believe that cultivated meat could eventually compete with conventional farming on price.

The basic science is relatively simple: cells are taken from a living animal and grown in large steel tanks known as bioreactors. The difficulty (3) ____ in doing this on an industrial scale. The nutrient solution in which the cells grow remains expensive, and keeping huge tanks free of contamination is a constant challenge. Several companies have already had to (4) ____ back their ambitions after discovering that their production costs were far higher than they had predicted.

Regulation is another (5) ____ block. Only a handful of countries have approved the sale of cultivated meat, and some have moved to ban it altogether, (6) ____ concerns about food safety and the livelihoods of traditional farmers.

Even so, supporters remain optimistic. They point out that early solar panels were also dismissed as a (7) ____ product before mass production brought prices down dramatically. Whether cultivated meat will follow the same path is far from certain, but the question is no longer whether it can be made; it is whether it can be made cheaply enough to (8) ____ a difference.

items.prompt: Gap (1)
items.explanation: 'Regard something as' es la estructura correcta. 'Deem' se usa sin 'as' ('deemed it a curiosity'), y 'reckon'/'believe' no admiten 'as' con complemento.

items.prompt: Gap (2)
items.explanation: 'Spring up' significa aparecer de repente y en gran número (empresas, edificios). 'Strike up' se usa con conversaciones o amistades, y 'jump up'/'leap up' significan levantarse de un salto.

items.prompt: Gap (3)
items.explanation: 'The difficulty lies in + -ing' es la colocación fija (la dificultad radica en). 'Rest with' se usa para responsabilidades, y 'stand'/'sit' no forman esta expresión.

items.prompt: Gap (4)
items.explanation: 'Scale back' (reducir el alcance) es transitivo y encaja con 'their ambitions'. 'Step back', 'fall back' y 'lie back' son intransitivos y no pueden llevar objeto directo.

items.prompt: Gap (5)
items.explanation: 'Stumbling block' es un obstáculo. 'Building block' existe, pero significa componente básico, lo contrario de lo que pide el contexto.

items.prompt: Gap (6)
items.explanation: 'Cite concerns' (alegar preocupaciones como motivo) es la colocación correcta. 'Quote' se usa con palabras textuales, 'claim' no encaja con 'concerns' y 'refer' necesitaría 'to'.

items.prompt: Gap (7)
items.explanation: 'A niche product' es un producto de nicho, dirigido a un mercado minoritario. 'Corner', 'margin' y 'border' no se usan como adjetivos con 'product'.

items.prompt: Gap (8)
items.explanation: La expresión fija es 'make a difference' (marcar la diferencia). Ninguno de los otros verbos se combina con 'difference' en este sentido.

sets.title: Micro-flats
sets.instructions: Read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
sets.passage:
As rents in major cities continue to rise, a growing number of young professionals are choosing to live in so-called micro-flats, some of (1) ____ measure barely twenty square metres. Developers claim that clever design makes up (2) ____ the lack of space: beds fold into walls, tables slide out from kitchen units and storage is hidden under the floor.

For residents (3) ____ spend most of their waking hours at the office or out with friends, this can be a reasonable trade-off. Living centrally means shorter commutes and easy access to restaurants, gyms and cultural venues. (4) ____ is more, many micro-flat buildings include shared lounges and rooftop terraces, which go some way towards compensating for the cramped private quarters.

Critics are less enthusiastic. They argue that, (5) ____ attractive the marketing may be, people need more than a bed and a kettle to lead healthy lives. Spending long periods in very small rooms has been linked to stress, and the problem became painfully obvious during periods (6) ____ residents were required to work from home.

There is also a concern that micro-flats allow developers to charge more per square metre (7) ____ they would for conventional apartments. Unless planning rules set minimum standards, cities could end up with housing that is profitable for builders but (8) ____ from ideal for the people who live in it.

items.prompt: Gap (1)
items.explanation: 'Some of which' introduce una relativa no especificativa referida a 'micro-flats'. Tras preposición no se puede usar 'that'.

items.prompt: Gap (2)
items.explanation: 'Make up for' es un phrasal verb que significa compensar.

items.prompt: Gap (3)
items.explanation: Pronombre relativo especificativo con función de sujeto, referido a personas ('residents').

items.prompt: Gap (4)
items.explanation: 'What is more' es un conector fijo que significa 'además'.

items.prompt: Gap (5)
items.explanation: 'However + adjetivo + sujeto + may be' expresa concesión: por muy atractivo que sea.

items.prompt: Gap (6)
items.explanation: Adverbio relativo de tiempo referido a 'periods'. 'In which' sería correcto pero son dos palabras.

items.prompt: Gap (7)
items.explanation: El comparativo 'more' exige 'than'.

items.prompt: Gap (8)
items.explanation: 'Far from ideal' es una expresión fija que significa 'nada ideal'.

sets.title: Managed by an algorithm
sets.instructions: Read the text below. Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.
sets.passage:
In warehouses, delivery firms and ride-hailing platforms, software now decides which tasks workers receive and how quickly they must complete them. Supporters praise the (1) ____ of these systems, which can allocate work far faster than any human supervisor.

Yet the people being managed often describe the experience in less flattering terms. Many complain that decisions are taken (2) ____ and that there is no one to appeal to when the system makes a mistake. A driver who is (3) ____ penalised for a late delivery caused by road works may find it almost impossible to have the decision reversed.

Researchers have also raised concerns about (4) ____. When every movement is tracked, workers may feel under constant pressure, and some studies suggest a link between intensive monitoring and higher rates of (5) ____.

Regulators are beginning to respond. Proposed legislation in several countries would oblige companies to explain the logic behind automated decisions, a requirement that many firms regard as (6) ____ because their algorithms are commercially sensitive. Others argue that greater (7) ____ would actually benefit employers by building trust.

What seems clear is that the spread of algorithmic management is (8) ____ in many sectors. The real question is whether it can be made fair.

items.prompt: EFFICIENT
items.explanation: Tras 'the' y antes de 'of' hace falta un sustantivo: efficient → efficiency.

items.prompt: ARBITRARY
items.explanation: Se necesita un adverbio que modifique a 'are taken': arbitrary → arbitrarily (la 'y' pasa a 'i').

items.prompt: FAIR
items.explanation: Adverbio con prefijo negativo: penalizar injustamente por un retraso que no fue culpa del conductor.

items.prompt: PRIVATE
items.explanation: Tras 'about' se necesita un sustantivo: private → privacy. El contexto de rastreo constante lo confirma.

items.prompt: ANXIOUS
items.explanation: Tras 'rates of' hace falta un sustantivo: anxious → anxiety (cambia la terminación interna).

items.prompt: WORK
items.explanation: Adjetivo negativo tras 'regard as': las empresas consideran el requisito inviable. Requiere prefijo 'un-' y sufijo '-able'. Palabras que no derivan de WORK (p. ej. 'impracticable') no son válidas.

items.prompt: OPEN
items.explanation: Tras 'greater' se necesita un sustantivo: open → openness (transparencia). Ojo con la doble 'n'.

items.prompt: REVERSE
items.explanation: El contexto ('the real question is whether it can be made fair') indica que la expansión de esta gestión no tiene vuelta atrás: prefijo 'ir-' y sufijo '-ible'.

sets.title: Key word transformations (Set 2)
sets.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.prompt: I regret not checking the figures before the presentation. || WISH || I ____ the figures before the presentation.
items.explanation: Para lamentar algo del pasado se usa 'wish + past perfect'.

items.prompt: The board is unlikely to approve the merger this year. || CHANCE || There is ____ the board approving the merger this year.
items.explanation: 'Unlikely' equivale a 'little chance of + sujeto + -ing'. No vale 'a little chance', que sugiere una posibilidad moderada.

items.prompt: Although the experiment was carefully planned, it failed. || SPITE || The experiment failed ____ carefully planned.
items.explanation: 'In spite of' va seguido de sustantivo o gerundio, así que se usa 'being' (o 'having been') con el participio 'planned'.

items.prompt: Nobody told the staff about the restructuring until the last minute. || KEPT || The staff ____ about the restructuring until the last minute.
accept: had been kept in the dark
items.explanation: 'Keep someone in the dark' significa no informar a alguien. En pasiva: 'were kept in the dark'.

items.prompt: Working from home is much less stressful than commuting every day. || NEARLY || Working from home is not ____ commuting every day.
items.explanation: 'Not nearly as + adjetivo + as' expresa una gran diferencia, igual que 'much less ... than'.

items.prompt: The analysts didn't expect the share price to rise so sharply. || TAKEN || The analysts were ____ the sharp rise in the share price.
items.explanation: 'Be taken by surprise by' / 'be taken aback by' expresan que algo pilló a alguien por sorpresa.

sets.title: Why the sensible thing feels so wrong
sets.instructions: You are going to read a magazine article about the psychology of saving and investing. For questions 1-6, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
sets.passage:
Why the sensible thing feels so wrong

Every January, my friend Lucía opens a spreadsheet, types in her savings, and closes it again without changing a thing. She knows, in the abstract, that the money sitting in her current account is quietly losing value to inflation. She has read the articles, nodded along to the podcasts, and even downloaded an investment app, which now lives in a folder on her phone labelled 'Later'. Lucía is not ignorant. She is, if anything, too well informed - and that, I have come to think, is precisely the problem.

The conventional explanation for financial inertia is a lack of knowledge. Teach people about compound interest, the argument goes, and they will behave accordingly. It is an appealing idea, not least because it flatters the people who make it: economists, educators and the burgeoning industry of personal-finance influencers. Yet the evidence that literacy alone changes behaviour is surprisingly thin. Studies of financial-education programmes tend to find that their effects are modest and fade within months, rather like the resolve of a new gym member.

What the knowledge model overlooks is that money is rarely just money. For Lucía, whose parents lost a small business in the 2008 crisis, cash in the bank is not an underperforming asset; it is a wall between her and a memory. To move it into the market would be to dismantle that wall brick by brick, and no chart showing long-run returns can make that feel safe. Behavioural economists have a name for part of this - loss aversion, the tendency to feel a loss roughly twice as keenly as an equivalent gain - but the label, useful as it is, risks making the phenomenon sound like a glitch to be patched rather than a story to be understood.

There is also the matter of choice. The modern saver faces not one decision but hundreds: which fund, which platform, which level of risk, which moment to begin. Each option carries the faint possibility of regret, and regret, unlike loss, attaches itself to the person who chose. If your cash is slowly eroded by inflation, you can blame the economy. If the market falls the week after you invest, you have only yourself to blame. Seen in this light, doing nothing is not laziness. It is a rational way of ensuring that, whatever happens, it will not be your fault.

None of this is to romanticise paralysis. The costs of staying in cash are real, if invisible, and they compound just as reliably as returns do. But if we want people to act differently, lecturing them about percentages is unlikely to get us very far. More promising are approaches that reduce the emotional weight of the first step: default enrolment in pension schemes, which turns inaction into investment; automatic monthly contributions, which spare savers from having to time the market; and advisers willing to ask about a client's history before asking about their risk tolerance.

I put some of this to Lucía over coffee. She listened politely, then pointed out - with some justification - that I had not exactly rushed to rebalance my own portfolio after the last downturn. It was a fair hit. Those of us who write about money are not immune to the forces we describe; we are simply better at dressing them up in jargon. Perhaps the most honest thing a financial commentator can admit is that knowing what to do and being able to do it are two entirely separate skills, and that only one of them can be taught in a classroom.

Lucía, for the record, has now set up a modest monthly transfer into an index fund. She describes it as 'small enough not to think about'. That, it turns out, may be the whole point.

items.prompt: In the first paragraph, the writer suggests that Lucía's failure to invest is
options: caused by a lack of reliable information.
made worse rather than better by what she knows.
the result of a distrust of financial technology.
typical of people who rely on podcasts for advice.
items.explanation: El autor dice que Lucía está 'too well informed' y que eso es 'precisely the problem': saber más no la ayuda, la paraliza. La A contradice el texto ('Lucía is not ignorant'); la C y la D no se mencionan.

items.prompt: What does the writer imply about the 'conventional explanation' in the second paragraph?
options: It is popular partly because it suits those who promote it.
It has been convincingly disproved by research.
It applies more to fitness than to personal finance.
It is rejected by most professional economists.
items.explanation: 'Not least because it flatters the people who make it' indica que la idea resulta atractiva porque favorece a quienes la defienden. La B exagera: la evidencia es 'surprisingly thin', no una refutación; el gimnasio es solo una comparación (C) y los economistas son quienes la defienden (D).

items.prompt: Why does the writer mention 'loss aversion' in the third paragraph?
options: to show that Lucía's behaviour is fully explained by economic theory
to argue that behavioural economists have misunderstood their research
to suggest that Lucía's fears could easily be corrected
to acknowledge a useful concept while warning against oversimplifying
items.explanation: El autor reconoce que la etiqueta es útil ('useful as it is') pero advierte que puede hacer que el fenómeno parezca un fallo técnico en vez de una historia personal. La A contradice 'a name for part of this'; la B no se dice; la C es justo lo que critica ('a glitch to be patched').

items.prompt: In the fourth paragraph, 'Seen in this light' refers to
options: the large number of decisions facing modern savers.
the likelihood of the market falling shortly after an investment.
the idea that people feel personally responsible for outcomes they chose.
the tendency of savers to blame the economy for their losses.
items.explanation: La expresión remite a la idea inmediatamente anterior: el arrepentimiento se asocia a quien decide, así que no decidir evita la culpa. La A es el tema del inicio del párrafo, no el punto que se retoma; B y D son ejemplos que ilustran la idea, no la idea misma.

items.prompt: How does the writer react to Lucía's comment in the sixth paragraph?
options: The writer accepts it as a fair criticism.
The writer dismisses it as irrelevant to the argument.
The writer takes offence at her lack of respect for financial experts.
The writer uses it to show that experts are less reliable than ordinary people.
items.explanation: 'With some justification' y 'It was a fair hit' muestran que acepta la crítica. La D es una trampa: dice que los comentaristas no son inmunes a esas fuerzas, no que sean menos fiables que el resto; nada indica que se ofenda (C) ni que la descarte (B).

items.prompt: What is the purpose of the final paragraph?
options: to suggest that Lucía has completely overcome her anxieties about money
to imply that small regular investments are rarely worthwhile
to admit that the writer's conversation with Lucía achieved nothing
to illustrate the value of reducing the emotional weight of a decision
items.explanation: La transferencia 'small enough not to think about' ejemplifica la propuesta del párrafo 5: reducir el peso emocional del primer paso. Nada indica que haya superado del todo sus miedos (A), y el desenlace es positivo, no inútil (B, C).

sets.title: Changing course: four career switches into finance
sets.instructions: You are going to read four people describing how they changed career. For questions 1-10, choose from the people (A-D). The people may be chosen more than once.
sets.passage:
A — Marta, former corporate lawyer, now an associate at a mid-market private equity fund
After six years drafting share purchase agreements, I realised I was more interested in why deals were happening than in the clauses that held them together. The move into private equity was less dramatic than people assume: lawyers already sit in the room when the big decisions are made. What I underestimated was the modelling. My first month involved late nights rebuilding a leveraged buyout model that a 23-year-old analyst could have done in his sleep, and I found that genuinely humbling. I took a pay cut to make the switch, which my parents still regard as madness, although carried interest could more than make up for it if the fund performs. The one thing I miss is the certainty of legal work: a contract is either right or wrong, whereas an investment thesis can be perfectly reasoned and still fail.

B — Daniel, former investment banker, now at a single-family office
Investment banking gave me an extraordinary education, but by my fourth year I could no longer remember the last time I had cooked dinner at home. When a headhunter mentioned a family office managing the wealth of an industrial family, I was sceptical - I assumed it would be glorified bookkeeping. In fact, the breadth is remarkable: on any given day I might be reviewing a direct stake in a vineyard, a co-investment alongside a buyout fund and the family's philanthropy budget. The pace is slower, and decisions are made over long lunches rather than in frantic conference calls. Some former colleagues think I have 'retired early', and I admit I sometimes feel the urge to prove them wrong. The real adjustment has been learning that the client is not a company but a family, with all the history and sensitivities that implies.

C — Priya, former engineer, now an analyst on a sustainable equity fund
I spent eight years designing wind turbines, so moving into an asset manager felt, at first, like a betrayal of my training. I soon discovered it was the opposite. Portfolio managers kept asking me questions that no financial analyst could answer - whether a company's claimed efficiency gains were physically plausible, for example. My technical background gave me credibility quickly, though I still had to pass the first level of a demanding professional qualification in my first year. What surprised me most was how much of the job is communication. A brilliant analysis is worthless if you cannot explain it to a client in three sentences. I had always thought of myself as too introverted for that kind of thing; now I present to pension-fund trustees twice a month and, to my astonishment, I enjoy it.

D — Tom, former auditor, now at an M&A boutique
Audit taught me to be suspicious of numbers, which turns out to be a very marketable habit. I left a large accountancy firm after three years to join a twelve-person boutique that advises family-owned companies on their sale. In a big firm, you are one of hundreds of people working for a client; here, I was on calls with company founders within my first fortnight. That exposure is exhilarating but also unforgiving - there is no one to hide behind if you get a figure wrong. The other surprise was how much selling we do. Boutiques live and die by their reputation, so even the most junior people are expected to help pitch for new mandates. If I had one piece of advice for anyone considering a similar move, it would be to talk to people already doing the job before you resign, not after. I did it the other way round.

items.prompt: Which person would do things in a different order if they could start again?
items.explanation: Tom aconseja hablar con profesionales antes de dimitir y admite: 'I did it the other way round'.

items.prompt: Which person had expected their new role to be narrower than it actually is?
items.explanation: Daniel pensaba que sería 'glorified bookkeeping' y descubrió que 'the breadth is remarkable'.

items.prompt: Which person admits struggling with a task that a less experienced colleague would find easy?
items.explanation: Marta reconstruyó un modelo LBO que 'a 23-year-old analyst could have done in his sleep' y lo encontró 'humbling'.

items.prompt: Which person was surprised to enjoy something they had thought did not suit their personality?
items.explanation: Priya se creía demasiado introvertida para presentar y ahora lo disfruta 'to my astonishment'.

items.prompt: Which person had direct contact with business owners very soon after joining?
items.explanation: Tom estaba en llamadas con fundadores 'within my first fortnight'. Marta habla de estar en la sala como abogada, no de contacto temprano con propietarios en su nuevo puesto.

items.prompt: Which person accepted a lower salary in order to change career?
items.explanation: Marta dice 'I took a pay cut to make the switch'. Nadie más menciona una reducción de ingresos.

items.prompt: Which person initially worried that the move went against their professional background?
items.explanation: Priya sintió al principio que era 'a betrayal of my training'.

items.prompt: Which person is sometimes tempted to show former colleagues that they misjudged the move?
items.explanation: Daniel siente 'the urge to prove them wrong' ante quienes creen que se ha jubilado pronto. Los padres de Marta no son antiguos colegas.

items.prompt: Which person misses the clear-cut nature of their previous job?
items.explanation: Marta echa de menos 'the certainty of legal work': un contrato está bien o mal, mientras que una tesis de inversión puede fallar.

items.prompt: Which person mentions that staff at every level contribute to winning new clients?
items.explanation: Tom: 'even the most junior people are expected to help pitch for new mandates'.

sets.title: C1 vocabulary in a finance context
sets.instructions: Choose the word or phrase (A, B, C or D) which best completes each sentence.

items.prompt: The CFO ____ the board's concerns about liquidity with a detailed cash-flow forecast.
items.explanation: La colocación fija es 'allay concerns/fears'. 'Console' y 'comfort' toman personas como objeto, no preocupaciones, y 'lighten' va con 'the load' o 'the mood'.

items.prompt: After months of negotiation, the acquisition ____ when the buyer failed to secure financing.
items.explanation: 'Fall through' = no llegar a concretarse un plan o acuerdo. 'Fall out' = discutir/enemistarse; 'fall back' = retroceder; 'fall behind' = retrasarse.

items.prompt: The analyst's revenue forecast turned out to be wide of the ____.
items.explanation: Modismo fijo 'wide of the mark' = muy desacertado. Las otras opciones no forman la expresión.

items.prompt: The ____ reason for the delay was inadequate due diligence.
items.explanation: 'Principal' (adjetivo) = principal. 'Principle' es un sustantivo (principio), confusión típica; 'principled' = con principios; 'principality' = principado.

items.prompt: The proposed merger has come under close ____ from the competition authorities.
items.explanation: 'Come under (close) scrutiny' es la colocación fija para el examen minucioso por parte de reguladores. 'Attention' y 'notice' se usan con otras estructuras ('pay close attention', 'come to the notice of'), y 'regard' significa consideración o estima.

items.prompt: With interest rates rising, many start-ups are struggling to keep their heads above ____.
items.explanation: 'Keep one's head above water' = sobrevivir con dificultades económicas. Las otras palabras no forman el modismo.

items.prompt: Following the poor results, the company was forced to ____ off 200 employees.
items.explanation: 'Lay off' = despedir por motivos económicos. 'Let off' = perdonar un castigo; 'put off' = aplazar; 'set off' = partir.

items.prompt: The country's ____ growth slowed sharply in the third quarter.
items.explanation: 'Economic' = relativo a la economía como sistema (economic growth). 'Economical' = que ahorra dinero o recursos, confusión muy frecuente; 'economy' y 'economics' son sustantivos y no forman esta colocación.

items.prompt: The fund has a ____ track record of successful exits in the healthcare sector.
items.explanation: 'A proven track record' es la colocación estándar. 'Tried and tested' es otra expresión que no encaja aquí.

items.prompt: Rather than ____ around the bush, the partner told us directly that the deal was off.
items.explanation: 'Beat around/about the bush' = andarse con rodeos. Ningún otro verbo forma el modismo.

items.prompt: Persistent inflation has ____ into households' disposable income.
items.explanation: 'Eat into' = reducir gradualmente (ahorros, beneficios, ingresos). 'Swallow' y 'digest' no se combinan con 'into' en este sentido, y 'chew' tiene sentido literal.

items.prompt: As stated in the terms and conditions, fees are ____ to change without prior notice.
items.explanation: 'Subject to change' es la fórmula contractual estándar. 'Exposed to' implica riesgo, 'inclined to' expresa tendencia de una persona y 'submitted' no forma esta expresión.

items.prompt: The start-up has ____ considerable interest from venture capital firms.
items.explanation: 'Attract interest' es la colocación natural. 'Lure' toma personas como objeto y sugiere engaño; 'pull' y 'drag' no se combinan con 'interest'.

items.prompt: Junior analysts are expected to learn the ____ within their first few weeks.
items.explanation: 'Learn the ropes' = aprender cómo funciona algo. 'Pull strings' es otro modismo (usar contactos).

items.prompt: After the stress test, the bank had to ____ up its capital position.
items.explanation: 'Shore up' = reforzar algo débil. 'Hold up' = retrasar o resistir; 'wind up' = liquidar una empresa; 'pin up' = colgar.

items.prompt: The founder's decision to sell was ____ by a sharp fall in the share price.
items.explanation: 'Prompt' = provocar o motivar una decisión. 'Promote' (ascender o promocionar) es un falso amigo frecuente; 'propped' (apuntalado) no encaja y 'prompting' no forma la pasiva.

items.prompt: There is only a ____ chance that the deal will close before the end of the year.
items.explanation: 'A slim chance' es la colocación natural. 'Meagre' va con 'salary' o 'resources', 'lean' con 'times' o 'year' y 'sparse' con 'population' o 'vegetation'.

items.prompt: After losing the mandate to a rival bank, the team went back to the ____ board.
items.explanation: 'Go back to the drawing board' = empezar de nuevo tras un fracaso. Es una expresión fija.

items.prompt: The government has announced plans to ____ down on tax evasion by offshore entities.
items.explanation: 'Crack down on' = tomar medidas duras contra algo. 'Break down' = averiarse o desglosar; 'knock down' = derribar; 'back down' = echarse atrás.

items.prompt: The new CEO's arrival has had a ____ impact on staff morale.
items.explanation: 'Considerable' = notable o significativo. 'Considerate' = atento con los demás, confusión clásica; 'considered' = meditado.

sets.title: Accounting & the Three Statements
sets.instructions: Choose the best answer (A, B, C or D). Assume a 25% tax rate unless stated otherwise, and assume that taxes are paid in cash in the same period. All figures in EUR millions.

items.prompt: Depreciation expense increases by 10. Tax rate is 25%. Walking through the three statements, what is the change in the company's cash balance at the end of the period?
items.explanation: Resultado neto: -10 x (1-0,25) = -7,5. En el estado de flujos se suma la amortización (no caja) +10, así que el CFO sube 2,5 por el ahorro fiscal (10 x 25%). El balance cuadra: PP&E -10, caja +2,5 (activo -7,5) y patrimonio -7,5.

items.prompt: A company writes down inventory by 20. The write-down is tax-deductible and the tax rate is 25%. What is the change in total assets?
items.explanation: Resultado neto -15 (20 x 0,75). CFO: -15 + 20 (ajuste no caja) = +5 de caja. Activo: inventario -20 y caja +5 = -15, igual a la caída del patrimonio. -20 olvida el ahorro fiscal en caja.

items.prompt: Holding everything else constant, which of the following increases cash flow from operating activities?
items.explanation: Una caída de cuentas a cobrar significa que se ha cobrado caja de clientes, lo que aumenta el CFO. Las otras tres opciones son aumentos de activos circulantes operativos o reducciones de pasivos operativos, que consumen caja.

items.prompt: Balance sheet data: receivables 120, inventory 80, payables 90, cash 50, short-term bank debt 40. What is operating (non-cash) net working capital?
items.explanation: El circulante operativo excluye caja y deuda financiera: 120 + 80 - 90 = 110. 160 incluye la caja; 120 incluye caja y deuda a corto; 70 resta la deuda sin incluir la caja.

items.prompt: Operating net working capital rises from 110 to 135 during the year. What is the impact on free cash flow?
options: No impact, because working capital is a balance sheet item
items.explanation: Un aumento del circulante operativo de 25 es una inversión de caja: reduce el FCF en 25. Lo que importa es la variación, no el saldo (135).

items.prompt: A company uses accelerated depreciation for tax purposes and straight-line depreciation in its financial statements. In the early years of the asset's life, this creates:
options: A permanent difference with no deferred tax
A reduction in reported tax expense below cash taxes
items.explanation: Al principio la amortización fiscal es mayor que la contable, así que se pagan menos impuestos hoy que el gasto fiscal contable: es una diferencia temporaria imponible que genera un pasivo por impuesto diferido. Revertirá en años posteriores.

items.prompt: Book pre-tax income is 400. Tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by 50 and there are no other differences. Tax rate 25%. What are the cash taxes payable for the year?
items.explanation: Base imponible = 400 - 50 = 350; impuesto corriente = 350 x 25% = 87,5. El gasto contable es 100 (400 x 25%) y la diferencia de 12,5 aumenta el pasivo por impuesto diferido.

items.prompt: Under IFRS 16, how is the principal portion of a lessee's lease payments classified in the cash flow statement?
options: It does not appear because it is non-cash
items.explanation: Con NIIF 16 la parte de principal del pago del arrendamiento se clasifica en actividades de financiación (como amortizar deuda). Por eso el CFO mejora frente al antiguo tratamiento de arrendamiento operativo, donde todo el alquiler restaba en operaciones.

items.prompt: A company previously expensed annual rent of 50 as an operating lease. Under IFRS 16 it recognises right-of-use depreciation of 40 and lease interest of 12. Compared with the old treatment, what is the change in EBIT?
items.explanation: EBITDA sube 50 (desaparece el alquiler). EBIT = EBITDA - amortización: +50 - 40 = +10. El interés (12) va por debajo del EBIT; el resultado antes de impuestos cae 2 (52 de gasto frente a 50), y +50 es el efecto en EBITDA, no en EBIT.

items.prompt: A buyer pays 500 for 100% of a target. The target's book net assets are 300 and the fair-value step-up on identifiable assets is 80. Ignoring deferred taxes, what goodwill is recognised?
items.explanation: Valor razonable de los activos netos identificables = 300 + 80 = 380. Fondo de comercio = 500 - 380 = 120. 200 olvida el ajuste a valor razonable; 380 son los activos netos, no el fondo de comercio.

items.prompt: How is goodwill treated in the individual accounts of a Spanish company reporting under the Plan General de Contabilidad (after the 2016 reform)?
options: It is never amortised and only tested for impairment, exactly as under IFRS
It is written off directly against equity on acquisition
It is amortised over its useful life, presumed to be 10 years unless otherwise shown, and also tested for impairment
It is amortised over a mandatory 20-year period with no impairment testing
items.explanation: Desde el RD 602/2016 el PGC exige amortizar el fondo de comercio según su vida útil, que se presume de 10 años salvo prueba en contrario, además de la prueba de deterioro. En las cuentas consolidadas bajo NIIF-UE no se amortiza: es una diferencia clave al comparar compañías españolas.

items.prompt: A company records a goodwill impairment of 40 that is not tax-deductible. What is the effect on cash flow from operating activities?
items.explanation: El resultado neto cae 40 (sin ahorro fiscal porque no es deducible), pero en el CFO se suma de nuevo el deterioro al ser un gasto no caja: -40 + 40 = 0. -30 supone erróneamente que es deducible.

items.prompt: Which inventory cost formula is NOT permitted under either IFRS or the Spanish PGC?
items.explanation: Tanto la NIC 2 como el PGC prohíben el LIFO. FIFO y coste medio ponderado están permitidos, y la identificación específica se usa para bienes no intercambiables.

items.prompt: Opening inventory is 200, purchases during the year are 900 and closing inventory is 250. What is cost of goods sold?
items.explanation: COGS = inventario inicial + compras - inventario final = 200 + 900 - 250 = 850. 950 suma el final en lugar de restarlo al inicial (900 + 250 - 200).

items.prompt: Ignoring taxes, a company capitalises 60 of development costs instead of expensing them; amortisation starts next year. In the current year, compared with expensing, which statement is correct?
options: EBITDA and total cash flow are both 60 higher
EBITDA is 60 higher, CFO is 60 higher, CFI is 60 lower and total cash flow is unchanged
EBITDA is unchanged but net income is 60 higher
CFO is 60 lower because the cost is now an investment
items.explanation: Capitalizar mueve el gasto del P&L al balance: EBITDA y CFO suben 60, pero el desembolso aparece como inversión en el CFI (-60). La caja total no cambia; sin impuestos, la decisión contable no altera la caja.

items.prompt: EBITDA 200, taxes on EBIT 30, capex 60, increase in operating working capital 15, interest expense 20. What is unlevered free cash flow (FCFF)?
items.explanation: FCFF = 200 - 30 - 60 - 15 = 95. El interés no se resta en el FCFF (es un flujo antes de financiación); 75 sí lo resta. 125 suma el circulante en lugar de restarlo, y 110 lo ignora.

items.prompt: A non-listed Spanish SME prepares individual accounts under the PGC and rents its offices under an operating lease. How does it account for the lease as lessee?
options: It recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability, as under IFRS 16
It records the rent as an expense in the P&L, with no right-of-use asset on the balance sheet
It capitalises the full future rent as PP&E
It records the rent directly against reserves
items.explanation: El PGC no ha adoptado la NIIF 16 para las cuentas individuales: el arrendatario en un arrendamiento operativo reconoce el alquiler como gasto. Al comparar su EBITDA con grupos que reportan bajo NIIF hay que ajustar los alquileres, o el EBITDA bajo NIIF estará inflado en términos relativos.

items.prompt: A company pays a cash dividend of 50. Which financial statement is NOT affected?
items.explanation: El dividendo es una distribución de beneficios, no un gasto: no pasa por la cuenta de resultados. Reduce caja y reservas (balance y estado de cambios en el patrimonio) y aparece como salida en financiación.

items.prompt: At the start of the year a company issues a 100 bond at 8% annual interest, paid in cash at year-end. Tax rate 25%; the proceeds are kept as cash and taxes are paid in cash within the year. What is the net change in cash over the year?
items.explanation: CFF +100 por la emisión. Intereses de 8 reducen el resultado neto en 8 x 0,75 = 6, que es el efecto neto en caja (pago de 8 menos ahorro fiscal de 2). Total: +100 - 6 = +94. 92 olvida el ahorro fiscal.

items.prompt: On 1 October a customer pays 120 upfront for a 12-month subscription. The financial year ends on 31 December. What deferred revenue balance is shown at year-end?
items.explanation: Se han prestado 3 de 12 meses: ingreso reconocido = 120 x 3/12 = 30. Los 90 restantes siguen siendo un pasivo (ingreso diferido) porque el servicio aún se debe al cliente.

sets.title: Valuation
sets.instructions: Choose the best answer (A, B, C or D). Figures in EUR millions unless stated otherwise. Recompute every figure before choosing.

items.prompt: Market value of equity 600, market value of debt 400, cost of equity 10%, pre-tax cost of debt 5%, tax rate 25%. What is the WACC?
items.explanation: WACC = 0,6 x 10% + 0,4 x 5% x (1 - 0,25) = 6,0% + 1,5% = 7,5%. 8,0% olvida el escudo fiscal de la deuda.

items.prompt: Risk-free rate 3%, levered beta 1.2, equity risk premium 5%. What is the cost of equity under CAPM?
items.explanation: Ke = 3% + 1,2 x 5% = 9,0%. 9,6% multiplica la beta por toda la rentabilidad de mercado (1,2 x 8%); 8,0% ignora la beta.

items.prompt: Free cash flow in year 5 (the final forecast year) is 100. WACC 8%, perpetual growth 2%. Using the Gordon growth method, what is the terminal value at the end of year 5?
items.explanation: VT = FCF5 x (1 + g) / (WACC - g) = 100 x 1,02 / 0,06 = 1.700. 1.666,7 olvida crecer el flujo un año (100/0,06); 1.275 divide entre WACC en lugar de WACC - g.

items.prompt: Year-5 EBITDA is 150 and you apply an 8.0x exit multiple. With a 10% WACC and end-of-year discounting, what is the present value of the terminal value (to one decimal)?
Year-1 free cash flow is 100 and WACC is 10%. Using the mid-year convention, what is its present value (to two decimals)?
items.explanation: Con la convención de mitad de año se descuenta 0,5 años: 100 / 1,1^0,5 = 100 / 1,04881 = 95,35. 90,91 es descuento de fin de año. La convención eleva el valor porque supone que la caja llega de forma repartida durante el año.

items.prompt: Which pairing of cash flow and discount rate is internally consistent?
options: FCFF discounted at the cost of equity to obtain equity value
FCFE discounted at the cost of equity to obtain equity value
FCFE discounted at WACC to obtain enterprise value
FCFF discounted at the cost of debt to obtain enterprise value
items.explanation: El FCFE es la caja disponible solo para el accionista, así que se descuenta al coste del capital (Ke) y da directamente el valor del equity. El FCFF (para todos los financiadores) se descuenta al WACC y da el enterprise value.

items.prompt: FCFF is 120, interest expense 20, tax rate 25%, and net new borrowing during the year is +10. What is FCFE?
items.explanation: FCFE = FCFF - intereses x (1 - t) + endeudamiento neto = 120 - 15 + 10 = 115. 110 olvida el escudo fiscal; 95 resta el nuevo endeudamiento en lugar de sumarlo.

items.prompt: Equity value 1,000; gross debt 400; cash 150; non-controlling (minority) interests 60; preferred shares 50; investments in associates 80. What is enterprise value?
items.explanation: EV = 1.000 + 400 - 150 + 60 + 50 - 80 = 1.280. Minoritarios y preferentes se suman; las participadas por puesta en equivalencia se restan porque su resultado no está en el EBITDA. 1.440 suma las participadas.

items.prompt: A DCF gives an enterprise value of 2,000. Net debt is 500, minority interests 100 and investments in associates 50. There are 50 million diluted shares. What is the implied value per share?
items.explanation: Equity = 2.000 - 500 - 100 + 50 = 1.450; por acción = 1.450 / 50 = 29,00 EUR. 27,00 resta las participadas en lugar de sumarlas (1.350/50); 28,00 las ignora (1.400/50).

items.prompt: Why are minority (non-controlling) interests added when moving from equity value to enterprise value?
options: Because minority shareholders rank ahead of debt holders
Because they are a form of cash
Because consolidated EBITDA includes 100% of subsidiaries that the parent does not fully own
Because IFRS classifies them as liabilities
items.explanation: Al consolidar se incluye el 100% del EBITDA de la filial aunque el grupo solo posea, por ejemplo, el 70%. Para que numerador y denominador sean coherentes, el EV debe incluir el valor de la parte de terceros. Bajo NIIF los minoritarios forman parte del patrimonio, no del pasivo.

items.prompt: Comparable companies trade at a median of 9.0x EV/EBITDA. The target's EBITDA is 50 and its net debt is 120 (no other bridge items). What is the implied equity value?
items.explanation: EV implícito = 9 x 50 = 450; equity = 450 - 120 = 330. 450 es el EV, no el equity; 570 suma la deuda neta en lugar de restarla.

items.prompt: A company has net income of 80 and 40 million shares outstanding. Its peer group trades at 15.0x P/E. What is the implied share price?
items.explanation: BPA = 80 / 40 = 2,00 EUR; precio = 15 x 2,00 = 30,00 EUR. 1.200 es el valor total del equity (15 x 80), no el precio por acción.

items.prompt: Why do precedent transaction multiples usually exceed trading comparable multiples for the same sector?
options: Precedent transactions use forward EBITDA while trading comps use historical EBITDA
Acquirers pay a control premium and often price in expected synergies
Precedent transactions exclude net debt from the calculation
Listed companies have lower risk than private targets
items.explanation: En una adquisición el comprador paga una prima de control y, a menudo, parte de las sinergias esperadas; los múltiplos de cotización reflejan participaciones minoritarias. Por eso las transacciones suelen marcar el extremo alto del rango en un football field.

items.prompt: Which valuation approach is most appropriate for a commercial bank?
options: P/TBV and P/E, or a dividend discount model
items.explanation: En un banco la deuda (depósitos) es materia prima del negocio y no financiación, así que EV, EBITDA y FCFF carecen de sentido. Se valora a nivel de equity: P/VC tangible (frente al ROTE), P/E o modelos de descuento de dividendos sujetos al capital regulatorio (CET1).

items.prompt: Which metric is specific to valuing life insurance companies?
items.explanation: El embedded value suma el patrimonio ajustado y el valor actual de los beneficios futuros de la cartera de pólizas en vigor, y es el indicador característico de las aseguradoras de vida. P/TBV se usa sobre todo en bancos; EV/EBITDAR en aerolíneas o retail.

items.prompt: You must value a fast-growing SaaS company with negative EBITDA and net income. Which multiple is most useful?
items.explanation: Con EBITDA y beneficio negativos, P/E y EV/EBITDA no tienen significado. Las compañías SaaS en crecimiento se comparan por EV/Ventas o EV/ARR, ajustando por crecimiento y márgenes (p. ej., la regla del 40).

items.prompt: Why is EV/EBITDA often preferred to P/E when comparing companies with very different leverage?
options: EBITDA includes interest expense, so leverage is captured
It is independent of capital structure because both EV and EBITDA belong to all capital providers
P/E cannot be calculated for leveraged companies
EV/EBITDA always gives a lower valuation
items.explanation: EV y EBITDA son métricas a nivel de empresa (antes de intereses), por lo que no dependen de cómo esté financiada. El P/E se ve afectado por el gasto financiero y por el apalancamiento, lo que distorsiona la comparación. El EBITDA no incluye intereses.

items.prompt: Share price EUR 20; 100 million basic shares; 10 million in-the-money options with a strike price of EUR 10. Using the treasury stock method, how many diluted shares are there?
items.explanation: Al ejercer las opciones se ingresan 10 x 10 = 100 M EUR, con los que se recompran 100 / 20 = 5 M acciones. Nuevas netas = 10 - 5 = 5 M; diluidas = 105 M. 110 M ignora la recompra.

items.prompt: In a DCF for a mature eurozone company with an 8% WACC, which terminal growth rate is most defensible?
options: Equal to the forecast-period revenue CAGR of 12%
items.explanation: El crecimiento a perpetuidad debe estar por debajo del crecimiento nominal a largo plazo de la economía (en torno a 2-3%) y siempre por debajo del WACC. Un 9% hace negativo el denominador (WACC - g) y un 6% genera un valor terminal desproporcionado.

items.prompt: Which of the following multiples is internally inconsistent?
items.explanation: El numerador y el denominador deben referirse a los mismos financiadores. El EV pertenece a todos (deuda y equity), pero el beneficio neto solo al accionista, ya que es después de intereses. EV/EBITDA y EV/EBIT son coherentes, y también P/E (equity/equity).

sets.title: LBO & Private Equity – Junior Analyst Technical Test
sets.instructions: Choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question. Work without a calculator: mental maths and reasonable approximations are expected. Unless stated otherwise, ignore fees and taxes.

items.prompt: A sponsor acquires a company with EBITDA of EUR 50m at an entry multiple of 10.0x EV/EBITDA. Transaction fees are EUR 20m. Debt is raised at 5.0x EBITDA. Assuming the target is acquired cash-free and debt-free, how much sponsor equity is required?
items.explanation: Usos: EV 500m (50 x 10) + comisiones 20m = 520m. Fuentes: deuda 250m (5 x 50) + equity. Equity = 520 - 250 = 270m. La trampa de 250m olvida que las comisiones también hay que financiarlas.

items.prompt: A PE fund invests EUR 100m and exits after 3 years receiving EUR 200m, with no interim cash flows. What is the approximate IRR?
items.explanation: 2x en 3 años: 2^(1/3) = 1,26, es decir, una TIR de aproximadamente 26%. El 33% sale de dividir el 100% de ganancia entre 3 años (interés simple), lo cual ignora la capitalización.

items.prompt: An investment returns 3.0x money-on-money over 5 years with a single exit cash flow. What is the approximate IRR?
items.explanation: 3^(1/5) es aproximadamente 1,246, es decir, una TIR de alrededor del 25%. El 40% resulta de dividir el 200% de ganancia entre 5 años (sin capitalización), un error típico.

items.prompt: Using the rule of 72, approximately how long does it take to double an investment compounding at 18% per year?
items.explanation: Regla del 72: 72 / 18 = 4 años. El valor exacto es ln2/ln1,18, aproximadamente 4,2 años, así que 4 es la mejor aproximación.

items.prompt: Entry: EBITDA EUR 40m, EV/EBITDA 8.0x, net debt EUR 200m. Exit after 5 years: EBITDA EUR 60m, EV/EBITDA 8.0x, net debt EUR 120m. What is the equity money multiple (MoM)?
items.explanation: Equity de entrada = 320 - 200 = 120m. Equity de salida = 480 - 120 = 360m. MoM = 360 / 120 = 3,0x.

items.prompt: Using the same deal (entry EBITDA 40m at 8.0x with net debt 200m; exit EBITDA 60m at 8.0x with net debt 120m), how much of the EUR 240m increase in equity value is explained by deleveraging?
items.explanation: La reducción de deuda neta es 200 - 120 = 80m (desapalancamiento). El crecimiento del EBITDA aporta 20 x 8 = 160m y la expansión de múltiplo es cero (8x a 8x). 160 + 80 = 240m.

items.prompt: Which value creation lever in an LBO is generally considered the least within the sponsor's control and therefore the least prudent to underwrite in the base case?
options: EBITDA growth through pricing and cost initiatives
Debt paydown from free cash flow
Add-on acquisitions bought at lower multiples
items.explanation: La expansión de múltiplo depende sobre todo de las condiciones de mercado en la salida, que el sponsor no controla; por eso el caso base suele asumir múltiplo de salida igual o inferior al de entrada. Las otras palancas son operativas o financieras y dependen más de la gestión.

items.prompt: A EUR 100m PIK note accrues interest at 10% per year, compounding annually, with nothing paid in cash. What is the amount owed at maturity after 3 years?
items.explanation: El PIK capitaliza los intereses: 100 x 1,1^3 = 133,1m. 130m sería interés simple (sin capitalizar), lo que no refleja cómo funciona un PIK.

items.prompt: Which description best fits a unitranche facility?
options: A single debt facility, typically provided by a direct lender or small club, that combines senior and subordinated risk at one blended interest rate
A senior secured bank loan syndicated to many banks with amortising tranches A and B
A subordinated instrument with equity warrants ranking below the senior debt
An unsecured high-yield bond listed on an exchange
items.explanation: El unitranche es una única facilidad con un tipo combinado que sustituye a la estructura senior + mezzanine, muy habitual en el mid-market europeo con fondos de direct lending. La opción C describe la deuda mezzanine; la B, un préstamo bancario sindicado tradicional.

items.prompt: What is the key difference between maintenance and incurrence covenants?
options: Maintenance covenants apply only to bonds; incurrence covenants apply only to bank loans

Maintenance covenants are tested periodically (e.g., quarterly) whatever the borrower does; incurrence covenants are tested only when the borrower takes a specified action, such as raising additional debt
Incurrence covenants are stricter because they are tested every month
Maintenance covenants restrict dividends, while incurrence covenants restrict capex
items.explanation: Los maintenance covenants (p. ej., ratio máximo de apalancamiento) se comprueban periódicamente; los incurrence solo se activan cuando la empresa realiza una acción concreta (endeudarse más, pagar dividendos). Un préstamo 'covenant-lite' carece de maintenance covenants.

items.prompt: A loan has a maximum net debt/EBITDA covenant of 5.0x. Net debt is EUR 360m and LTM EBITDA is EUR 80m. Holding net debt constant, by what percentage can EBITDA fall before the covenant is breached?
items.explanation: Apalancamiento actual = 360 / 80 = 4,5x. El incumplimiento se produce con un EBITDA inferior a 360 / 5 = 72m. Caída permitida = 8 / 80 = 10%. El 11,1% es cuánto podría aumentar la deuda neta con el EBITDA constante (de 360m a 400m, es decir, 40/360), no cuánto puede caer el EBITDA.

items.prompt: A portfolio company raises new debt to pay a special dividend to the PE fund (a dividend recap). What is the most direct effect on the fund's reported metrics at the moment of the recap, ignoring fees?
options: TVPI rises because the new debt is added to NAV
DPI increases while TVPI is broadly unchanged, as value moves from unrealised NAV to distributions
DPI falls because the fund's commitment increases
items.explanation: El dividendo es una distribución: sube el DPI, pero el NAV de la participación baja en la misma cuantía (la empresa tiene más deuda), por lo que el TVPI apenas cambia. Suele mejorar la TIR al adelantar flujos, pero aumenta el apalancamiento de la empresa.

items.prompt: A EUR 400m fund charges 2.0% per year on committed capital during a 5-year investment period, then 1.5% per year on invested capital of EUR 300m for the following 5 years. What are total management fees over the 10 years?
items.explanation: Años 1-5: 2% x 400 = 8m/año x 5 = 40m. Años 6-10: 1,5% x 300 = 4,5m/año x 5 = 22,5m. Total = 62,5m. 80m supondría un 2% sobre el comprometido durante 10 años.

items.prompt: A fund has returned all EUR 100m of contributed capital and generated total profits of EUR 80m. The preferred return owed to LPs is EUR 30m, carry is 20% and there is a 100% GP catch-up. How much carried interest does the GP receive?
items.explanation: Cascada: los LPs reciben 30m de preferente; el catch-up al 100% da al GP X tal que X/(30+X) = 20%, es decir, X = 7,5m; los 42,5m restantes se reparten 80/20 (8,5m para el GP). Total GP = 7,5 + 8,5 = 16m = 20% de 80m. La trampa de 10m aplica el 20% solo al exceso sobre el hurdle (sin catch-up).

items.prompt: What best explains the 'J-curve' in private equity fund returns?
options: Funds deliberately overvalue assets in early years
In early years, management fees, deal costs and conservative valuations depress returns before value creation and exits push them up
The J-curve reflects the fall in interest rates over a fund's life
It describes the declining management fee rate after the investment period
items.explanation: Al principio se pagan comisiones y costes y las inversiones se valoran prudentemente (a coste), por lo que la TIR es negativa; luego, la creación de valor y las salidas generan la curva ascendente en forma de J.

items.prompt: An LP has paid in EUR 200m to a fund, received distributions of EUR 150m, and the remaining NAV of its interest is EUR 170m. What are the DPI and TVPI?
items.explanation: DPI = distribuciones / desembolsado = 150 / 200 = 0,75x. TVPI = (distribuciones + NAV) / desembolsado = (150 + 170) / 200 = 1,60x. 0,85x sería el RVPI (170/200).

items.prompt: In a GP-led secondary using a continuation vehicle, what typically happens?
options: An LP sells its entire fund interest to another LP without GP involvement
The GP transfers one or more assets from an existing fund into a new vehicle it also manages, and existing LPs can choose to sell for cash or roll over
The GP lists the fund on a stock exchange
The portfolio company buys back the sponsor's shares using new debt
items.explanation: En un continuation vehicle el GP sigue gestionando el activo durante más tiempo, entra capital nuevo de secundarios y los LPs existentes eligen entre liquidez o reinversión. La opción A describe un secundario LP-led; la D, una recompra o recap.

items.prompt: An LP sells a fund interest with NAV of EUR 50m at 92% of NAV. The interest also carries EUR 10m of unfunded commitments, which the buyer assumes. How much cash does the buyer pay the seller at closing?
items.explanation: Precio = 92% x 50 = 46m. El compromiso no desembolsado no se paga al vendedor: el comprador lo asume y lo aportará al fondo cuando haya capital calls. 56m suma erróneamente el unfunded al precio.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes a typical difference between a single-family office making direct investments and a traditional closed-end PE fund?
options: Family offices must exit every investment within 5 years to return capital to LPs
Family offices typically invest permanent capital with no fixed fund life, allowing longer holding periods and often lower leverage
Family offices always charge 2 and 20 to the family
PE funds have no time constraints on their exits
items.explanation: El family office invierte capital propio y permanente, sin vida fija del fondo ni LPs externos que exijan devolución, por lo que puede mantener inversiones mucho más tiempo y con menos apalancamiento. El fondo cerrado suele tener una vida de unos 10 años y presión por salir.

items.prompt: A portfolio company has EBITDA of EUR 100m, capex of EUR 20m, cash interest of EUR 30m, cash taxes of EUR 15m and an increase in net working capital of EUR 5m. How much free cash flow is available for debt repayment?
items.explanation: FCF = 100 - 20 - 30 - 15 - 5 = 30m. Un aumento del circulante consume caja, por lo que se resta. 35m olvida el circulante; 45m olvida los impuestos; 50m olvida los impuestos y el circulante.

sets.title: M&A – Junior Analyst Technical Test
sets.instructions: Choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question. Ignore transaction fees unless stated otherwise.

items.prompt: An acquirer has net income of EUR 200m, 100m shares and a share price of EUR 40 (P/E 20x). It buys a target with net income of EUR 50m for EUR 900m, paid entirely in new acquirer shares. Ignoring synergies, what is the effect on the acquirer's EPS?
items.explanation: Nuevas acciones = 900 / 40 = 22,5m. BPA combinado = 250 / 122,5 = 2,041 frente a 2,00: acreción de alrededor del 2,0%. Coherente con la regla: P/E del comprador (20x) mayor que el P/E pagado (18x).

items.prompt: An acquirer has net income of EUR 300m and 150m shares (EPS EUR 2.00). It buys a target with net income of EUR 40m for EUR 600m, financed fully with new debt at 6% pre-tax; tax rate is 25%. Ignoring synergies, what is the EPS impact?
items.explanation: Interés después de impuestos = 600 x 6% x 0,75 = 27m. Nuevo beneficio = 300 + 40 - 27 = 313m; BPA = 313/150 = 2,087, alrededor de un +4,3%. +1,3% olvida el escudo fiscal (resta 36m); +13,3% ignora el coste de la deuda.

items.prompt: In an all-stock acquisition, ignoring synergies and fees, the deal is EPS-accretive when:
options: The target's P/E paid is lower than the acquirer's P/E
The target's P/E paid is higher than the acquirer's P/E
The target has higher revenue growth than the acquirer
The acquirer's share price is below book value
items.explanation: Si el comprador cotiza a un P/E superior al pagado por la target, emite relativamente pocas acciones por cada euro de beneficio adquirido, y el BPA sube. El crecimiento de ingresos no determina la acreción contable inmediata.

items.prompt: An acquirer buys a target at 25x earnings, funded entirely with debt at 6% pre-tax interest; the tax rate is 25%. Ignoring synergies, the deal is most likely:
options: Accretive, because 6% is below the acquirer's cost of equity
Dilutive, because the target's earnings yield (4%) is below the after-tax cost of debt (4.5%)
Neutral, because debt does not affect EPS
items.explanation: Rendimiento del beneficio de la target = 1/25 = 4%. Coste de la deuda después de impuestos = 6% x (1 - 25%) = 4,5%. Como 4% < 4,5%, el beneficio adquirido no cubre los intereses: es dilutiva.

items.prompt: An acquirer has net income of EUR 100m, 50m shares (EPS EUR 2.00) and a share price of EUR 30. It buys a target with net income of EUR 20m for EUR 400m in stock. With a 25% tax rate, approximately what pre-tax synergies are needed for the deal to be EPS-neutral?
items.explanation: Nuevas acciones = 400/30 = 13,33m; total 63,33m. Beneficio necesario = 2,00 x 63,33 = 126,67m frente a 120m: faltan 6,67m después de impuestos, es decir, 6,67/0,75 = 8,9m antes de impuestos. 6,7m es la cifra post-tax, no la pedida.

items.prompt: Why do buyers and their lenders usually give more credit to cost synergies than to revenue synergies?
options: Cost synergies are generally more within management's control and easier to quantify and achieve
Revenue synergies cannot be included in a valuation under accounting rules
Revenue synergies always take longer than ten years to materialise
items.explanation: Las sinergias de costes (duplicidades, compras, oficinas) dependen sobre todo de decisiones internas; las de ingresos dependen de clientes y competidores, por lo que son más inciertas. No hay ninguna prohibición contable de incluirlas en la valoración.

items.prompt: Which sequence best reflects a typical sell-side auction process?
options: CIM, teaser, NDA, LOI, IOI, SPA
Teaser, NDA, CIM, IOI, due diligence and management presentations, binding offer/LOI, SPA
NDA, SPA, teaser, CIM, IOI, LOI
Teaser, IOI, NDA, SPA, CIM, LOI
items.explanation: Primero el teaser anónimo, después el NDA para acceder al CIM, la oferta indicativa (IOI), el acceso al data room y a la dirección, la oferta vinculante/LOI y finalmente la negociación y firma del SPA.

items.prompt: Which statement about an Indication of Interest (IOI) is correct?
options: It is a binding offer that obliges the bidder to close
It is a non-binding first-round bid, often a valuation range based on the CIM, used to shortlist bidders
It is signed only after the SPA
It is the confidentiality agreement signed before receiving the teaser
items.explanation: La IOI es indicativa y no vinculante; el vendedor la usa para seleccionar a los pujadores que pasan a la segunda ronda. El acuerdo de confidencialidad es el NDA.

items.prompt: In a sell-side process, which document is typically sent to potential buyers before they sign an NDA?
options: The draft SPA with full disclosure schedules
items.explanation: El teaser es un resumen breve, normalmente sin nombre, que despierta el interés. El CIM y el data room contienen información confidencial y solo se comparten tras firmar el NDA.

items.prompt: Under a locked box mechanism:
options: The price is adjusted after closing based on actual net debt and working capital at completion
The equity price is fixed by reference to a historical balance sheet date, economic risk passes to the buyer from that date, and the buyer is protected by leakage provisions
The buyer pays nothing until an earn-out target is reached
The seller keeps all profits generated until completion
items.explanation: En el locked box el precio se fija sobre un balance de referencia y no hay ajuste posterior; el comprador se protege prohibiendo la 'leakage' (salidas de valor al vendedor). La opción A describe completion accounts.

items.prompt: A deal uses a locked box with an agreed equity price of EUR 200m. After the locked box date, the target paid a EUR 3m dividend to the seller (not permitted) and EUR 1m of management fees that the SPA lists as permitted leakage. How much can the buyer recover from the seller?
items.explanation: Solo la leakage no permitida (el dividendo de 3m) da derecho a reclamación, normalmente euro por euro. La leakage permitida (1m) ya se tuvo en cuenta en el precio.

items.prompt: A deal uses completion accounts. Agreed EV is EUR 500m and the target normalised working capital (NWC) is EUR 60m. At completion, net debt is EUR 110m and NWC is EUR 55m. What is the final equity price?
items.explanation: Equity = EV - deuda neta + (NWC real - NWC objetivo) = 500 - 110 + (55 - 60) = 385m. 390m olvida el déficit de circulante; 395m suma el ajuste con el signo contrario; 335m resta todo el circulante real (55m) en lugar de solo la desviación frente al objetivo.

items.prompt: An earn-out pays the seller EUR 2 for every EUR 1 of year-2 EBITDA above EUR 20m, capped at EUR 10m. Year-2 EBITDA is EUR 24m. What is the earn-out payment?
items.explanation: Exceso = 24 - 20 = 4m; pago = 2 x 4 = 8m, por debajo del tope de 10m. El earn-out sirve para salvar diferencias de valoración vinculando parte del precio al rendimiento futuro.

items.prompt: From the acquirer's perspective, which is a genuine advantage of paying with its own shares rather than cash?
options: It never dilutes existing shareholders' ownership
It shares with the target's shareholders the risk that synergies or performance fall short
It always results in a lower tax bill for the acquirer
It removes the need for due diligence
items.explanation: Con acciones, los vendedores pasan a ser accionistas y asumen parte del riesgo del combinado. A cambio, el pago en acciones diluye la participación de los accionistas actuales, y puede interpretarse como señal de que el comprador cree que sus acciones están caras.

items.prompt: What is the main purpose of a Quality of Earnings (QoE) report in financial due diligence?
options: To audit the target's statutory accounts for regulatory filing
To assess the sustainability of historical earnings by normalising EBITDA for non-recurring, one-off and out-of-period items
To value the target using a DCF
To review the target's employment contracts
items.explanation: El QoE ajusta el EBITDA reportado para obtener un EBITDA normalizado y recurrente, que es la base del precio. No es una auditoría ni una valoración, y la revisión de contratos laborales corresponde a la due diligence legal o de RR. HH.

sets.title: Markets, Fintech & Mental Maths – Junior Analyst Test
sets.instructions: Choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question. Use mental maths; no calculator.

items.prompt: A bond has a modified duration of 6. If its yield rises by 50 basis points, its price will change by approximately:
items.explanation: Variación aproximada del precio = -duración modificada x variación del rendimiento = -6 x 0,5% = -3%. Precio y rendimiento se mueven en sentido contrario.

items.prompt: Which of the following bonds has the highest duration?
items.explanation: Un cupón cero tiene duración Macaulay igual a su vencimiento (10 años). Cualquier cupón adelanta flujos y reduce la duración, y un vencimiento más corto también la reduce.

items.prompt: A 1-year zero-coupon bond with face value 100 yields 5%. What is its price?
items.explanation: Precio = 100 / 1,05 = 95,24. 95,00 sería descontar restando el 5% al nominal, lo cual no es correcto para un rendimiento compuesto.

items.prompt: A bond with a 4% coupon has a yield to maturity of 5%. It trades:
options: At a price that cannot be determined from this information
items.explanation: Si el cupón (4%) es menor que el rendimiento exigido (5%), el precio debe estar por debajo de la par para compensar. Cupón por encima del YTM implica cotizar con prima.

items.prompt: An inverted yield curve means:
options: Long-term yields are above short-term yields
Short-term yields are above long-term yields, often read as the market expecting future rate cuts and weaker growth
Corporate bond yields are below government yields
items.explanation: La curva invertida (corto por encima de largo) refleja expectativas de bajadas de tipos y se ha asociado históricamente a recesiones. La curva normal tiene pendiente positiva.

items.prompt: A Spanish bank's mortgage book is mainly variable-rate, linked to Euribor. A sustained series of ECB rate cuts will most likely:
options: Compress its net interest margin as loan yields reprice down faster than deposit costs can fall
Have no effect, because mortgages are long-term
Increase the bank's interest income on the mortgage book
items.explanation: Con hipotecas variables, los ingresos por intereses bajan cuando bajan Euribor y los tipos del BCE, mientras que el coste de los depósitos ya era bajo y no puede caer en la misma proporción: el margen de intereses se comprime.

items.prompt: European leveraged loans used in LBOs typically pay interest as:
options: A fixed coupon set at issuance for the life of the loan
Euribor plus a margin, so lower ECB rates reduce the borrower's cash interest cost
A share of the company's revenue
The ECB deposit rate minus a spread
items.explanation: Los préstamos apalancados son de tipo variable (Euribor + diferencial). Por eso las bajadas de tipos del BCE mejoran el flujo de caja de las empresas participadas y favorecen las valoraciones de las LBO.

items.prompt: The risk-free rate is 3%, a stock's beta is 1.2 and the equity risk premium is 5%. Using CAPM, what is the cost of equity?
items.explanation: Ke = 3% + 1,2 x 5% = 3% + 6% = 9%. 9,6% resulta de multiplicar (3% + 5%) por 1,2, aplicando la beta también al tipo libre de riesgo.

items.prompt: If the equity risk premium demanded by investors rises while the risk-free rate is unchanged, then, all else equal:
options: Equity valuations rise because expected returns are higher
Equity valuations fall because future cash flows are discounted at a higher cost of equity
items.explanation: Una prima de riesgo mayor eleva el coste del capital propio, y descontar los mismos flujos a una tasa más alta reduce su valor actual. Es la rentabilidad esperada futura la que sube, no el precio actual.

items.prompt: A share price rises by 25% and then falls by 20%. What is the overall change?
items.explanation: 1,25 x 0,80 = 1,00, es decir, sin variación. Sumar porcentajes (+25 - 20 = +5%) es la trampa clásica.

items.prompt: A portfolio falls by 50%. What return is needed to get back to its original value?
items.explanation: Si 100 baja a 50, para volver a 100 hay que duplicar: +100%. Las pérdidas requieren subidas proporcionalmente mayores para recuperarse.

items.prompt: Revenue doubles from EUR 100m to EUR 200m over 6 years. What is the approximate CAGR?
items.explanation: Por la regla del 72, duplicar en 6 años implica unos 72/6 = 12% anual (exacto: 2^(1/6) - 1 = 12,2%). 17% sale de dividir el 100% entre 6 años (crecimiento simple).
